entities.name: PMID:10735686
observations: In pigs undergoing 3 hours of CPB, cooling to 28°C and rewarming to normothermia, biologically variable pulsatile CPB reduced mean SjvO2 <50% exposure versus conventional pulsatile CPB: 3.6±7.3 vs 82±96 %·min, p=0.004; cumulative exposure 42±87 vs 983±1158 %·min, p=0.004.
The intervention restored beat-to-beat rate/pressure variability and respiratory rhythms; groups had comparable temperature, MAP, blood gases, and hemoglobin.

entities.name: PMID:9456096
observations: In pigs cooled to 28°C and rewarmed during CPB, computer-controlled biologically variable pulsatile bypass reduced mean SjvO2 <50% exposure versus conventional apulsatile CPB: 1.9±3.6 vs 164±209 %·min, p=0.021; cumulative exposure 23±45 vs 1796±2263 %·min, p=0.020.
Temperature, rewarming rate, arterial gases, MAP, and hemoglobin were comparable between groups.

entities.name: Biovariable pulsation and SjvO2
observations: Two direct pig CPB comparisons consistently found less severe and shorter SjvO2 decline below 50% during rewarming with biologically variable pulsation than with conventional pulsatile or apulsatile bypass.
Direct human evidence was not identified; human studies of conventional pulsatility or higher pump flow are indirect.
